source_text: Πληγὰς αὐτοῖς, καὶ θανάτους, καὶ κολάσεων ἀνηκέστων πεῖ ραν ἐπανετείνετο. Καὶ ὁ μὲν τοιαῦτα, τὰ δὲ τῶν μαρτύρων ὁποῖα; Τί, φησὶ, δελεάζεις ἡμᾶς, ὦ θεο μάχε, ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ δουλεύειν δαίμοσιν ὀλεθρίοις, προτεινόμενος ἡμῖν τὰ σὰ ἀγαθά; Τί τοσοῦτον δίδως, ὅσον ἀφελέσθαι σπουδάζεις; Μισῶ δωρεὰν ζημίας πρόξενον· οὐ δέχομαι τιμὴν ἀτιμίας μητέρα. Χρήματα δίδως τὰ ἀπομένοντα, δόξαν τὴν ἀπανθοῦσαν. Γνώριμον ποιεῖς βασιλεῖ, ἀλλὰ τοῦ ὄντος βασιλέως ἀλλοτριοῖς. Τί μικρολόγως ὀλίγα τῶν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου προτείνεις; Ὅλος ἡμῖν ὁ κόσμος καταπεφρόνηται. Οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν τῆς ἐπιθυμουμένης ἐλπίδος ἀντάξια τὰ ὁρώμενα. Ὁρᾷς τὸν οὐρανὸν τοῦ τον, ὡς καλὸς ἰδεῖν, ὡς δὲ μέγας; καὶ τὴν γῆν, ἡλίκη; καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ θαύματα; Οὐδὲν τούτων ἐξισοῦται τῇ μακαριότητι τῶν δικαίων. Ταῦτα μὲν γὰρ παρέρχεται· τὰ δὲ ἡμέτερα μένει. Μιᾶς ἐπι θυμῶ δωρεᾶς, τοῦ στεφάνου τῆς δικαιοσύνης· περὶ μίαν δόξαν ἐπτόημαι, τὴν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρα νῶν. Φιλότιμός εἰμι πρὸς τὴν ἄνω τιμήν· κόλασιν δέδοικα τὴν ἐν τῇ γεέννῃ. Πῦρ ἐκεῖνό μοι φοβερόν· τὸ δὲ παρ' ὑμῶν ἀπειλούμενον ὁμόδουλόν ἐστιν. Οἶδεν αἰδεῖσθαι τοὺς εἰδώλων καταφρονοῦντας. Βέλη νη πίων λογίζομαι τὰς πληγὰς ὑμῶν. Σῶμα γὰρ τύπτεις· ὅπερ, ἐὰν μὲν ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἀντίσχῃ, λαμπρότερον στεφανοῦται, ἐὰν δὲ θᾶττον ἀπαγορεύση, οἴχεται ἀπαλλαγὲν δικαστῶν οὕτω βιαίων, οἳ, σωμάτων ὑπηρεσίαν παραλαβόντες, ἔτι καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν κατ άρχειν φιλονεικεῖτε· οἵ γε, εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν προτιμηθείητε, ὡς τὰ ἔσχατα ὑβρισμένοι παρ' ἡμῶν, χαλεπαίνετε, καὶ τὰς φοβερὰς ταύτας κολάσεις ἐπανατείνεσθε, ἔγκλημα ἡμῖν ἐπάγοντες τὴν εὐσέβειαν. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐ δειλοῖς, οὐδὲ φιλοζώοις, οὐδ' εὐκαταπλήκτοις ἐντεύξεσθε, ὑπὲρ τῆς εἰς Θεὸν ἀγάπης. Οἵδε ἡμεῖς καὶ τροχίζεσθαι, καὶ στρεβλοῦσθαι, καὶ καταπίμπρασθαι, καὶ πᾶν εἶδος βασανιστηρίων ἕτοιμοι καταδέχεσθαι. Ἐπεὶ δὲ τούτων ἤκουσεν ὁ ἀλαζὼν ἐκεῖνος καὶ βάρβαρος, οὐκ ἐνεγκὼν τῶν ἀνδρῶν τὴν παῤῥησίαν, ὑπερζέσας τῷ θυμῷ, ἐσκόπει τίνα ἂν ἐξεύροι μηχα νὴν, ὥστε μακρόν τε αὐτοῖς καὶ πικρὸν ὁμοῦ κατα σκευάσαι τὸν θάνατον. Εὗρε δὴ οὖν ἐπίνοιαν, καὶ σκοπεῖτε ὡς χαλεπήν. Περισκεψάμενος γὰρ τὴν φύσιν τῆς χώρας, ὅτι κρυμώδης, καὶ τὴν ὥραν τοῦ ἔτους, ὅτι χειμέριος, νύκτα ἐπιτηρήσας ἐν ᾗ μάλιστα τὸ δεινὸν ἐπιτείνεται, ἄλλως δὲ καὶ τότε βορέου αὐτὴν ἐπιπνέοντος, ἐκέλευσε πάντας γυμνωθέντας ὑπὸ τὸ αἴθριον ἐν μέσῃ τῇ πόλει πηγνυμένους ἀπο θανεῖν. Πάντως δὲ ἴστε, οἱ πεπειραμένοι χει μῶνος, ὡς ἀφόρητόν ἐστι τῆς βασάνου τὸ εἶδος. Οὐδὲ γὰρ δυνατὸν ἄλλοις ἐνδείξασθαι ἢ τοῖς προαποκείμενα ἔχουσιν ἐκ τῆς πείρας αὐτῆς τῶν λεγομένων τὰ ὑποδείγματα. Σῶμα γὰρ κρύει παραπεσὸν πρῶτον μὲν ὅλον ἐστὶ πελιδνὸν, πηγνυμένου τοῦ αἵματος· ἔπειτα κλονεῖται καὶ ἀναβράσσεται, ὀδόντων ἀρασσομένων, σπωμένων δὲ τῶν ἰνῶν, καὶ παντὸς τοῦ ὄγκου ἀπροαιρέτως συνελκομένου. Ὀδύνη δέ τις δριμεῖα, καὶ πόνος ἄῤῥητος αὐτῶν καθικνούμενος τῶν μυελῶν, δυσφορωτάτην ποιεῖται τοῖς πηγνυμένοις τὴν αἴσθησιν. Ἔπειτα ἀκρωτηριάζεται, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ πυρὸς, καιομένων τῶν ἄκρων. Ἀποδιωκόμενον γὰρ τὸ θερμὸν ἀπὸ τῶν περάτων τοῦ σώματος, καὶ συμφεῦγον ἐπὶ τὸ βάθος, τὰ μὲν, ὅθεν ἀπέστη, νεκρὰ καταλείπει, τὰ δὲ, ἐφ' ἃ συνωθεῖται, ὀδύναις δί δωσι, κατὰ μικρὸν τοῦ θανάτου διὰ τῆς πήξεως προσιόντος.
thought_title: The martyrs' bold reply and the ruler's freezing sentence
orientation: The Forty Martyrs are answering the ruler who has just tried flattery and threats, and now he threatens blows and death.
pass_a_gloss: He held out to them blows, and deaths, and trial of incurable punishments. And he such things, but the things of the martyrs of what sort? Why, they say, do you bait us, O fighter against God, to depart from the living God, and to serve destructive demons, holding out to us your good things? Why do you give so much as you are eager to take away? I hate a gift that procures loss; I do not accept honor that is mother of dishonor. You give money that remains behind, glory that fades. You make known to the king, but you alienate from the king who truly is. Why do you meanly hold out few of the things of the world? The whole world has been despised by us. The things seen are not equal in worth to the hope we desire. Do you see this heaven, how beautiful to see, and how great? and the earth, how large? and the wonders in it? None of these is made equal to the blessedness of the righteous. For these things pass away; but our things remain. I desire one gift, the crown of righteousness; I am excited about one glory, the one in the kingdom of heaven. I am ambitious for the honor above; I fear the punishment in hell. That fire is fearful to me; but the fire threatened by you is fellow-servant. It knows to show reverence to those who despise idols. I count your blows as arrows of infants. For you strike the body; which, if it holds out longer, is crowned more brightly, but if it gives up sooner, it departs, freed from judges so violent, who, having received service over bodies, still strive to rule also over souls; who, if you are not preferred even to our God, as utterly insulted by us, you are angry, and you hold out these fearful punishments, bringing against us as charge the devotion. But indeed you will not encounter cowardly, nor life-loving, nor easily terrified men, for the love toward God. We know both to be racked, and to be tortured, and to be burned, and to accept every kind of torture devices ready. But when that arrogant and barbarous man heard these things, not bearing the boldness of the men, boiling over with rage, he considered what device he might find, so as to prepare for them a death both long and bitter at once. He found then a plan, and see how harsh. For having examined the nature of the region, that it is frosty, and the season of the year, that it is wintry, having watched for a night in which especially the terrible thing is intensified, and besides also then the north wind blowing upon it, he commanded all, stripped naked, under the open sky in the middle of the city, freezing, to die. And you all know, those who have experienced winter, how unbearable is the form of the torture. For it is not possible to show to others except to those who have examples of the things said laid up beforehand from experience itself. For a body fallen into cold first is all livid, the blood freezing; then it is shaken and seethes, teeth striking together, the sinews convulsing, and the whole mass involuntarily contracting. And a sharp pain, and unspeakable labor reaching to the very marrows, makes the sensation most hard to bear for those freezing. Then it is mutilated at the extremities, as if by fire, the ends burning. For the heat being driven away from the limits of the body, and fleeing together to the depth, leaves dead the parts from which it departed, and gives to pains the parts to which it is crowded, death approaching little by little through the freezing.

lemmas.gloss: you bait, you entice with bait
he held out threateningly, he threatened with
has been despised, is held in contempt

choices.term: Πληγὰς αὐτοῖς, καὶ θανάτους, καὶ κολάσεων ἀνηκέστων πεῖραν ἐπανετείνετο
choices.english: He held out to them blows, and deaths, and trial of incurable punishments
choices.why: ἐπανατείνω means to hold out threateningly; πεῖραν is 'trial/experience' as object of the threatening gesture
rejected: He threatened them with blows, deaths, and experience of incurable punishments

choices.term: Τί, φησὶ, δελεάζεις ἡμᾶς, ὦ θεομάχε
choices.english: Why, they say, do you bait us, O fighter against God
choices.why: δελεάζω is specifically baiting with a lure, matching the flattery and gifts just offered; θεομάχε is vocative address
rejected: Why do you entice us, O enemy of God
Why do you lure us, O God-fighter

choices.english: I hate a gift that procures loss
choices.why: πρόξενος is one who procures or brings about; the gift is personified as causing loss
rejected: I hate a gift that is a loss-bringer
I hate a gift that brings damage

choices.why: ἀπανθέω means to lose its flower, to fade; the participle is present, emphasizing ongoing fading

choices.term: Ὁρᾷς τὸν οὐρανὸν τοῦτον, ὡς καλὸς ἰδεῖν, ὡς δὲ μέγας;
choices.english: Do you see this heaven, how beautiful to see, and how great?
choices.why: The rhetorical question with ὡς exclamatory clauses is preserved; τοῦτον is deictic 'this'
rejected: You see this heaven, how beautiful to see and how great

choices.term: τὸ δὲ παρ' ὑμῶν ἀπειλούμενον ὁμόδουλόν ἐστιν
choices.english: but the fire threatened by you is fellow-servant
choices.why: ὁμόδουλος means fellow-slave/fellow-servant; the martyrs demote the persecutors' fire to the same created order as themselves
rejected: but the fire you threaten is a fellow-slave
but what you threaten is of the same servile order

choices.english: It knows to show reverence to those who despise idols
choices.why: The subject is the fire of hell just mentioned (πῦρ ἐκεῖνο), which knows to respect those who despise idols; αἰδεῖσθαι is middle/passive infinitive of reverence
rejected: It knows how to respect those who despise idols
That fire knows to revere those who despise idols

choices.term: Βέλη νηπίων λογίζομαι τὰς πληγὰς ὑμῶν
choices.english: I count your blows as arrows of infants
choices.why: λογίζομαι with double accusative means 'I reckon X as Y'; νηπίων is genitive plural of infants
rejected: I consider your blows to be children's arrows
I reckon your blows as infant arrows

choices.term: οἵ γε, εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν προτιμηθείητε, ὡς τὰ ἔσχατα ὑβρισμένοι παρ' ἡμῶν, χαλεπαίνετε
choices.english: who, if you are not preferred even to our God, as utterly insulted by us, you are angry
choices.why: προτιμηθείητε is passive optative: 'you are preferred/honored above'; the judges are angry when not given precedence over God
rejected: who, if our God is not preferred even to you, as grossly insulted by us, you are angry

choices.term: Ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐ δειλοῖς, οὐδὲ φιλοζώοις, οὐδ' εὐκαταπλήκτοις ἐντεύξεσθε
choices.english: But indeed you will not encounter cowardly, nor life-loving, nor easily terrified men
choices.why: ἐντεύξεσθε is future middle of ἐντυγχάνω, 'you will meet/encounter'; the dative adjectives describe the men as objects encountered
rejected: But you will not find us cowardly, nor life-loving, nor easily terrified

choices.term: Οἴδαμεν ἡμεῖς καὶ τροχίζεσθαι, καὶ στρεβλοῦσθαι, καὶ καταπίμπρασθαι
choices.english: We know both to be racked, and to be tortured, and to be burned
choices.why: τροχίζεσθαι is specifically being put on the wheel; στρεβλοῦσθαι is being tortured on the rack; καταπίμπρασθαι is being burned up
rejected: We know how to be wheeled, and twisted, and burned

choices.why: ὑπερζέω means to boil over; τῷ θυμῷ is dative of respect or instrument, the rage being the medium of boiling

pass_b_english: He held out to them blows, and deaths, and the trial of incurable punishments. And what did the martyrs do in response? “Why do you bait us, fighter against God,” they said, “to abandon the living God and serve destructive demons by offering us your goods? Why do you give as much as you are eager to take away? I hate a gift that procures loss. I do not accept honor that is the mother of dishonor. You give money that remains behind, glory that fades. You make us known to the emperor, but you alienate us from the true King. Why do you offer us the little things of the world in such a stingy way? We have despised the whole world. The things that are seen are not worth the hope we long for. Do you see this heaven, how beautiful to see, and how great? And the earth, how vast? And the wonders in it? None of these equals the blessedness of the righteous. For these things pass away, but what is ours remains. I long for one gift: the crown of righteousness (2 Timothy 4:8). I am in a flutter about one glory: the glory in the kingdom of heaven. I am ambitious for the honor above. I fear the punishment in hell. That fire is fearful to me, but the fire threatened by you is a fellow-servant. It knows how to show reverence to those who despise idols. I count your blows as arrows of infants. For you strike the body; if it holds out longer, it is crowned more brightly, but if it gives up sooner, it departs, freed from such violent judges—you who, having received the service of bodies, still strive to rule over souls as well. And even though you are not preferred to our God, you are angry, as if you had been grossly insulted by us, and you hold out these fearful punishments, bringing against us the charge of devotion. But indeed you will not encounter cowardly men, nor life-loving men, nor easily terrified men, when it comes to love for God. We are ready to be racked, and tortured, and burned, and to accept every kind of torment. When that arrogant barbarian heard these things, he could not bear the men’s boldness. Boiling over with rage, he considered what device he might devise to make their death both long and bitter at the same time. He found a plan—and see how cruel it was. He examined the nature of the region, that it was freezing, and the season of the year, that it was winter. He watched for a night when the cold was at its worst, and when the north wind was blowing upon it. Then he commanded them all to be stripped naked and to die freezing under the open sky in the middle of the city. You all know, who have experienced winter, how unbearable this kind of torture is. It is not possible to describe it to others except to those who already have examples of what is said from their own experience. For a body that has fallen into cold is first all livid, as the blood freezes. Then it shudders and seethes, teeth chattering, fibers convulsing, and the whole mass involuntarily contracting. A sharp pain and unspeakable suffering reaches to the very marrow, and makes the sensation most distressing for those who are freezing. Then the extremities are destroyed, as if by fire, as the ends burn. For the heat is driven away from the extremities of the body and flees together to the depths. It leaves dead the parts from which it has departed, and gives pain to the parts into which it is crowded, as death approaches little by little through the freezing.

problems.quote: It knows to show reverence to those who despise idols.
problems.why: Subject is the fire threatened by the ruler, not idols. Fire knows how to be reverenced by idol-despisers, i.e., it serves the faithful.
problems.fix: It knows how to reverence those who despise idols.
problems.ruling: Οἶδεν αἰδεῖσθαι: fire knows how to be reverenced by idol-despisers, not 'show reverence to' them. Subject/object reversed.

problems.quote: you who, having received authority over bodies, still strive to rule over souls as well.
problems.source_quote: οἳ, σωμάτων ὑπηρεσίαν παραλαβόντες, ἔτι καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν κατάρχειν φιλονεικεῖτε
problems.why: ὑπηρεσίαν means 'service/ministry,' not 'authority.' They received a service over bodies, not authority over them.
problems.fix: you who, having received a service over bodies, still strive to rule over souls as well
problems.ruling: ὑπηρεσία means service, ministry, attendance—not authority. 'Received authority over bodies' misrepresents the Greek.

problems.quote: We know how to be racked, and tortured, and burned, and to accept every kind of torment.
problems.source_quote: Οἵδε ἡμεῖς καὶ τροχίζεσθαι, καὶ στρεβλοῦσθαι, καὶ καταπίμπρασθαι, καὶ πᾶν εἶδος βασανιστηρίων ἕτοιμοι καταδέχεσθαι
problems.why: English 'We know how to be' weakens ἕτοιμοι ('ready/willing'); 'know how' suggests capability, not readiness.
problems.fix: 'We are ready to be racked, and tortured, and burned, and to accept every kind of torment.'
problems.ruling: ἕτοιμοι means 'ready/willing'; 'know how to be' implies capability, losing readiness nuance.

edits.new: It knows how to reverence those who despise idols.

edits.old: you who, having received authority over bodies, still strive to rule over souls as well.

fixed: Changed 'It knows to show reverence to those who despise idols' to 'It knows how to reverence those who despise idols' because the subject is the fire, not idols; the fire knows how to reverence (serve) those who despise idols.
Changed 'authority over bodies' to 'a service over bodies' because the Greek ὑπηρεσίαν means service/ministry, not authority.
Changed 'We know how to be racked' to 'We are ready to be racked' because the Greek ἕτοιμοι means ready/willing, not capable.

problems.why: 'Infants' misses the force; νήπιοι means children/infants, but 'arrows of infants' is absurd—means weak, harmless weapons.

problems.quote: If you are not preferred even to our God, you are angry
problems.source_quote: εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν προτιμηθείητε, ὡς τὰ ἔσχατα ὑβρισμένοι παρ' ἡμῶν, χαλεπαίνετε
problems.why: Condition is 'if you are not preferred even to our God' — i.e., unless you outrank God; current rendering inverts the sense.
problems.fix: Unless you are preferred even to our God, you are angry
problems.ruling: Greek: 'if you are not preferred even to our God' = unless you outrank God; English inverts to 'if you are not preferred even to our God' as if God is preferred over you.

problems.quote: having received a service over bodies
problems.why: 'Service over bodies' is unclear; ὑπηρεσία here means jurisdiction/authority, not service performed.
problems.ruling: ὑπηρεσίαν means service/ministry, not jurisdiction; 'service over bodies' misleads readers about authority claimed.

edits.old: If you are not preferred even to our God, you are angry
edits.new: Unless you are preferred even to our God, you are angry

edits.old: having received a service over bodies

fixed: Βέλη νηπίων: νήπιοι means infants/children, but the phrase is figurative for weak, harmless weapons; 'children' is more natural and still literal.
εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν προτιμηθείητε: the condition is 'unless you are preferred even to our God,' so 'Unless' is correct.
σωμάτων ὑπηρεσίαν παραλαβόντες: ὑπηρεσία here means jurisdiction/authority, not service performed, so 'authority over bodies' is correct.

problems.why: "νηπίων" means infants/babies, not children generally; "arrows of infants" is the biblical idiom (Psalm 76:3 LXX).

problems.quote: Unless you are preferred even to our God, you are angry
problems.source_quote: οἵ γε, εἰ μὴ καὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν προτιμηθείητε, ὡς τὰ ἔσχατα ὑβρισμένοι παρ' ἡμῶν, χαλεπαίνετε
problems.why: Greek conditional is contrary-to-fact: "even if you are not preferred to our God, you are angry as if grossly insulted"; English inverts logic.
problems.fix: And even though you are not preferred to our God, you are angry, as if grossly insulted by us

problems.quote: It knows how to reverence those who despise idols.
problems.why: Subject is the fire threatened by the ruler, not 'it' generically; fire knows how to be reverenced by idol-despisers.
problems.fix: It knows how to be reverenced by those who despise idols.
problems.ruling: αἰδεῖσθαι is middle/passive 'to be reverenced,' not active 'to reverence'; fire is object of reverence.

problems.quote: you who, having received authority over bodies
problems.why: "ὑπηρεσίαν" means service/ministry, not authority; the martyrs mock the judges' limited role as servants of bodies.
problems.fix: you who, having received the service of bodies
problems.ruling: ὑπηρεσίαν means 'service/ministry,' not 'authority'; martyrs mock judges as mere body-servants, changing the meaning.
